description: Recurring day-to-day problems of undergraduate and graduate students around classes, deadlines, group projects, campus life, money, and dorm living.

items.title: Deadlines scattered across five course platforms
items.problem: Each course posts assignments in a different place (Canvas, a professor's website, email, a syllabus PDF), so students miss due dates they never saw in one list.
items.workaround: manually copying every syllabus into a calendar or notes app at the start of term

items.title: Syllabus dates changed mid-semester
items.problem: Professors shift due dates verbally in class or in a buried announcement, so the calendar the student built in week one is quietly wrong.
items.who: students who plan from the syllabus
items.workaround: asking classmates in the group chat 'wait, is that still due Friday?'

items.title: Three exams landing in the same week
items.problem: Students only realize in week 9 that midterms for three classes fall within two days, leaving no time to study for each properly.
items.workaround: cramming, or asking a professor for an extension after the fact

items.title: Big assignment not broken into steps
items.problem: A 20-page paper due in six weeks feels unstartable, so nothing happens until three days before and the whole thing is written in a panic.
items.workaround: all-nighters; vague intentions to 'start early'

items.title: Submitting the wrong file version
items.problem: Students upload a draft instead of the final, or the wrong file entirely, and only notice after the portal locks.
items.workaround: emailing the professor begging to resubmit

items.title: Missing the 11:59 PM submission cutoff
items.problem: Uploads at 11:58 fail because the file is too large or the portal is slow, and the assignment is marked late by a minute.
items.who: students who work up to the deadline
items.workaround: screenshotting the upload error as evidence for the professor

items.title: Not knowing current grade in a class
items.problem: Weighted categories, dropped lowest scores, and ungraded items make it impossible to tell whether a student is at a B+ or a C, so they can't decide where to focus.
items.who: students tracking GPA or scholarship thresholds
items.workaround: building a spreadsheet from the syllabus weighting, often wrong

items.title: What score is needed on the final
items.problem: Before the final exam students want to know the minimum score to keep their letter grade, and have to recompute weights by hand every time.
items.workaround: generic 'final grade calculator' websites that ignore dropped scores

items.title: Building a conflict-free class schedule
items.problem: Choosing sections that satisfy degree requirements, avoid time overlaps, avoid 8 AM slots, and leave gaps for work takes hours of trial and error.
items.workaround: paper grids, multiple browser tabs, and screenshots of the catalog

items.title: Waitlisted class seat opens unnoticed
items.problem: A seat in a full required class opens for a few hours and is gone again before the student happens to refresh the registration page.
items.workaround: refreshing the enrollment page dozens of times a day

items.title: Degree requirements progress is opaque
items.problem: Students can't easily see which requirements are complete, which courses double-count, and whether they'll graduate on time, until an advisor meeting months away.
items.workaround: a printed degree audit and a hand-maintained checklist

items.title: Choosing professors with no reliable info
items.problem: Students pick sections blind, relying on outdated or gamed rating sites, and end up with a grader or teaching style that wrecks their term.
items.workaround: asking friends and reading Rate My Professors

items.title: Lecture notes hard to review later
items.problem: Handwritten and typed notes from a fast lecture are disorganized, incomplete, and impossible to search when it's time to study.
items.workaround: borrowing a friend's notes or rewatching the recorded lecture

items.title: Recorded lectures too long to rewatch
items.problem: Reviewing for an exam means scrubbing through hours of 75-minute recordings to find the one part that was confusing.
items.who: students in courses with recorded lectures
items.workaround: watching at 2x speed

items.title: Making flashcards eats study time
items.problem: Turning slides and readings into flashcards takes so long that students run out of time to actually review them.
items.who: students in memorization-heavy courses (bio, languages, law)
items.workaround: Quizlet sets made by strangers that don't match the course

items.title: No practice problems for this specific course
items.problem: Textbook problems don't match what the professor tests, and past exams are hoarded or unavailable.
items.workaround: Chegg, frat test banks, or begging older students

items.title: Finding an empty study spot
items.problem: During midterms every library seat, study room, and outlet is taken, and students wander between buildings for half an hour.
items.workaround: arriving at 7 AM or texting friends to hold a seat

items.title: Booking a library study room
items.problem: Study room reservation systems are clunky, rooms get no-showed and sit empty while others are locked out.
items.workaround: squatting in rooms and hoping the booker doesn't show

items.title: Phone distraction during study sessions
items.problem: Students sit down to study and lose an hour to TikTok and group chats without noticing.
items.workaround: Forest app, phone in another room, or nothing

items.title: Can't find a study partner for a class
items.problem: Students in a hard class don't know anyone in it and have no way to find others who want to study together.
items.workaround: awkwardly asking neighbors in lecture or posting in a Discord

items.title: Office hours conflict with other classes
items.problem: The only time a student can get help from a professor or TA overlaps another class or a shift, so questions go unanswered for weeks.
items.workaround: long email threads or Piazza posts that get answered late

items.title: Group member goes silent before deadline
items.problem: One teammate stops responding days before the due date, and the rest have no idea whether their part is coming or must be redone.
items.workaround: frantic messages, then doing the work themselves at 2 AM

items.title: Unclear who is doing which part
items.problem: Group projects are divided verbally in one meeting, then two people do the same section while a third section is forgotten.
items.workaround: a pinned message in the group chat nobody rereads

items.title: Finding a meeting time for six people
items.problem: Coordinating a group meeting across six class schedules, jobs, and time zones takes a week of back-and-forth polls.
items.workaround: When2meet links and endless 'does Tuesday work?' messages

items.title: No record of who actually contributed
items.problem: When peer evaluations come, students can't prove a freeloader did nothing, and the freeloader gets the same grade.
items.workaround: screenshots of the group chat sent to the professor

items.title: Merging five different document versions
items.problem: Each member writes their section in a different tool and format, and someone spends the last night stitching them into one consistent document.
items.workaround: one person copy-pasting everything into a single Google Doc

items.title: Group chat scattered across apps
items.problem: One group uses iMessage, another WhatsApp, another Discord, another Slack, and important messages and files get lost between them.
items.who: students in multiple groups per term
items.workaround: searching four apps to find the file someone sent

items.title: Running out of money before month end
items.problem: Loan or allowance money arrives in a lump and is gone by week three, leaving students eating ramen until the next disbursement.
items.who: students on loans, stipends, or allowances
items.workaround: vague mental budgeting; borrowing from friends

items.title: Textbooks cost hundreds per term
items.problem: Required textbooks cost $100-300 each, and students don't know until week two whether the professor will actually use them.
items.workaround: pirated PDFs, library reserves, older editions, or skipping the book

items.title: Reselling used textbooks for almost nothing
items.problem: Bookstore buyback pays a fraction of the price while other students on campus would pay more, but there's no easy way to match them.
items.workaround: Facebook groups and taped flyers

items.title: Unused meal plan swipes expire
items.problem: Students pay for meal plans, then lose dozens of swipes or dining dollars at the end of each week or semester.
items.workaround: buying cases of snacks in the last week, or giving swipes away

items.title: Splitting costs with roommates
items.problem: Rent, utilities, toilet paper, and shared groceries are paid by whoever happened to be there, and nobody knows who owes whom.
items.workaround: Splitwise, Venmo requests, or letting it slide and resenting it

items.title: Scholarship deadlines slip by
items.problem: Dozens of small scholarships have different deadlines and requirements, and students miss most of them because tracking is too much work.
items.workaround: a bookmarked list that is never revisited

items.title: Finding which student discounts apply
items.problem: Software, transit, streaming, and local businesses offer student discounts, but students only find out by accident after paying full price.
items.workaround: UNiDAYS and word of mouth

items.title: Balancing part-time shifts with classes
items.problem: Work schedules change weekly and collide with labs, exams, and study time, and the student has no single view to spot the conflicts.
items.workaround: two separate calendars and hoping

items.title: Unexpected university fees on the bill
items.problem: Tuition statements include lab fees, tech fees, and health fees the student never saw coming, and it's unclear which can be waived.
items.workaround: calling the bursar's office and waiting on hold

items.title: Roommate chores never get done
items.problem: Dishes pile up, trash overflows, and the bathroom goes uncleaned because nobody agreed on whose turn it is.
items.who: students in dorms and shared apartments
items.workaround: passive-aggressive notes and one person doing everything

items.title: Laundry machines all taken
items.problem: Students haul laundry down to the basement to find every machine in use, or return to find their clothes dumped on the floor.
items.workaround: going at 6 AM; some campuses have machine-status apps that rarely work

items.title: Forgetting laundry in the machine
items.problem: Students start a load, get absorbed in something else, and come back hours later to wrinkled or removed clothes.
items.workaround: setting a phone timer, usually forgotten

items.title: Roommate schedule and quiet hours clash
items.problem: One roommate has an 8 AM class and the other games until 3 AM; neither knows the other's schedule so conflicts happen daily.
items.workaround: arguments or a whiteboard on the door

items.title: Finding a compatible roommate or subletter
items.problem: Students need a roommate for next year or someone to take their lease over summer, and matching happens through random Facebook posts with strangers.
items.workaround: Facebook housing groups and campus bulletin boards

items.title: Shared groceries disappear from the fridge
items.problem: Food bought by one roommate is eaten by another, and nobody tracks what is shared versus personal.
items.workaround: labels with names on them; mini-fridge in the bedroom

items.title: Moving out every summer
items.problem: Students must pack, store, and move everything they own every May and August, and forget what's in storage or what they need to buy again.
items.workaround: storage companies and a pile of unlabeled boxes

items.title: Dorm maintenance requests vanish
items.problem: A broken heater or leaking sink is reported through a clunky portal and no one knows if or when it will be fixed.
items.workaround: reporting again, or bothering the RA

items.title: Missing the campus shuttle
items.problem: Shuttle and campus bus times are unreliable, and students either wait 20 minutes in the cold or watch it leave as they arrive.
items.who: students on large or multi-campus universities
items.workaround: leaving far too early, or walking

items.title: Hearing about campus events after they happen
items.problem: Club meetings, free food events, and guest talks are announced on flyers and in emails students never read, so they find out the next day.
items.workaround: Instagram follows and a bloated inbox

items.title: Dining hall menu and crowding unknown
items.problem: Students walk across campus to a dining hall only to find a menu they don't want or a 30-minute line.
items.workaround: checking a PDF menu that's often outdated

items.title: Campus email overload
items.problem: The university sends dozens of newsletters, reminders, and announcements daily, and the one important message about a registration hold is buried.
items.workaround: ignoring the inbox and missing things

items.title: Making friends as a transfer or commuter
items.problem: Students who don't live in dorms or arrived after freshman year have no natural way to meet people and feel isolated.
items.workaround: joining clubs at random

items.title: Finding a ride home for breaks
items.problem: Students without cars need rides to the airport or hometown at holiday breaks and rely on chance posts to find someone going the same way.
items.workaround: Facebook rideshare groups and expensive Ubers

items.title: Gym and rec center overcrowded
items.problem: Students show up to the campus gym at peak time and every rack and treadmill is taken.
items.workaround: guessing off-peak hours

items.title: Lost campus printing and parking rules
items.problem: Students don't know where they can print, how many pages are free, or which lot they can park in without a ticket.
items.workaround: asking around and getting fined

items.title: Sleep schedule wrecked by late nights
items.problem: Assignments and social life push bedtime to 3 AM, then students sleep through 9 AM lectures and fall behind.
items.workaround: energy drinks and five alarms

items.title: Eating badly on a student budget
items.problem: Students with tiny kitchens, no time, and little money end up on instant noodles and takeout, and don't know cheap easy meals.
items.workaround: same three meals on repeat

items.title: Counseling center booked out for weeks
items.problem: When stress peaks during exams, the campus counseling center has a three-week wait and students don't know other options.
items.workaround: friends, or nothing

items.title: Tracking internship applications
items.problem: Students apply to 50+ internships with different deadlines, portals, and follow-up steps and lose track of where each stands.
items.workaround: a spreadsheet that gets abandoned

items.title: Keeping citations formatted correctly
items.problem: Every paper needs APA or MLA citations, and students lose points on formatting or spend hours fixing reference lists.
items.workaround: Zotero, citation generators with wrong output

items.title: Forgetting to log volunteer or co-curricular hours
items.problem: Programs and scholarships require documented hours, and students reconstruct months of activity from memory at the deadline.
items.who: students in honors, service, or scholarship programs
items.workaround: guessing and hoping no one checks

items.title: Registration holds discovered on registration day
items.problem: A missing immunization form or an unpaid $15 fee blocks course registration and the student finds out when the classes fill.
items.workaround: checking the portal repeatedly the week before

items.title: Reading load impossible to plan
items.problem: Weekly reading assignments across courses add up to hundreds of pages and students can't judge how long each will take.
items.workaround: skimming or skipping readings

items.title: Wasting the gaps between classes
items.problem: Students have scattered 50-minute gaps across the day that are too short to go home and end up scrolling instead of working.
items.workaround: none
